items.q: A current of 0.5 A flows through a resistor of 12 ohms. Calculate the voltage across it in volts.
Three resistors of 6, 10 and 12 ohms are connected in series. Find the total resistance in ohms.
items.s: R total = 6 + 10 + 12 = 28 ohms.

items.q: An appliance rated 5 kW is used for 2 hours. Calculate the energy consumed in kilowatt hours.
items.s: Energy = power x time = 5 x 2 = 10 kWh.

items.q: At a junction, currents of 6 A and 2 A enter while 4 A leaves along one branch. Find the current in the remaining outgoing branch in amperes.
items.s: Current leaving = current entering, so I = 6 + 2 - 4 = 4 A.

items.q: A series loop contains a 24 V source and resistive drops of 4 V and 3 V. Find the voltage across the remaining element in volts.
items.s: Remaining drop = 24 - 4 - 3 = 17 V.

items.q: A capacitor of 10 microfarads is connected across 200 V. Find the charge stored in millicoulombs.
Capacitors of 10 and 47 microfarads are joined in parallel. Find the total capacitance in microfarads.
items.s: C total = 10 + 47 = 57 microfarads.

items.q: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 100 V. Find its root mean square value in volts.
items.s: Vrms = Vpeak/root 2 = 100/1.414 = 70.71 V.

items.q: An alternating current has a root mean square value of 20 A. Find its peak value in amperes.
items.s: Ipeak = Irms x root 2 = 20 x 1.414 = 28.28 A.

items.q: Two resistors of 4 ohms and 4 ohms are connected in parallel. Calculate the equivalent resistance in ohms.
A potential divider of 40 ohms and 60 ohms is connected across a 12 V supply. Calculate the voltage appearing across the second resistor in volts.
A resistor of 12 ohms carries a current of 2 A. Calculate the power dissipated in watts.
items.s: P = I squared R = 2 x 2 x 12 = 48 W.

items.q: A source of 36 V with an internal resistance of 3 ohms supplies a load of 6 ohms. Using Thevenin's theorem, find the load current in amperes.
A source has a Thevenin voltage of 30 V and a Thevenin resistance of 12 ohms. Calculate the maximum power that can be transferred to a variable load, in watts.
items.s: Pmax = Vth squared/(4 Rth) = 900/(4 x 12) = 18.75 W.

items.q: A Norton equivalent consists of a current source of 5 A in parallel with 10 ohms. Find the Thevenin voltage of the equivalent source in volts.
items.s: Vth = I Norton x R Norton = 5 x 10 = 50 V.

items.q: Two sources act on a branch. Source A alone produces 6 A and source B alone produces 2 A in the opposite direction. Find the magnitude of the resultant current in amperes.
items.s: Resultant = 6 - 2 = 4 A in the direction of source A.

items.q: Two branches feed a common node, 9 V through 6 ohms and 9 V through 3 ohms. Using nodal analysis, find the node voltage in volts.
A capacitor of 400 microfarads is charged to 100 V. Calculate the energy stored in joules.
items.s: W = half C V squared = 0.5 x 400 x 10^-6 x 100 x 100 = 2 J.

items.q: An inductor of 50 mH carries a current of 10 A. Calculate the energy stored in its magnetic field in joules.
items.s: W = half L I squared = 0.5 x 50 x 10^-3 x 10 x 10 = 2.5 J.

items.q: Two capacitors of 6 and 4 microfarads are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in microfarads.
items.s: C = (C1 x C2)/(C1 + C2) = (6 x 4)/(6 + 4) = 2.4 microfarads.

items.q: An RC circuit uses a resistor of 10 kilohms and a capacitor of 100 microfarads. Calculate the time constant in seconds.
A coil of inductance 50 mH has a resistance of 50 ohms. Calculate its time constant in milliseconds.
A capacitor charges from 100 V through a resistor and one time constant has elapsed. Find the voltage across the capacitor at that instant in volts.
The current in an inductive circuit falls from 5 A and one time constant has elapsed. Find the current at that instant in amperes.
A sine wave has a peak value of 240 V. Calculate its average value over one half cycle in volts.
A coil of inductance 0.5 H is connected to a 60 Hz supply. Calculate its inductive reactance in ohms.
A capacitor of 22 microfarads is connected to a 60 Hz supply. Calculate its capacitive reactance in ohms.
A series circuit has a resistance of 4 ohms and a reactance of 8 ohms. Find its impedance in ohms.
items.s: Z = root of (R squared + X squared) = root of (16 + 64) = 8.94 ohms.

items.q: In a series circuit the resistance is 10 ohms and the inductive reactance is 6 ohms. Find the phase angle by which the current lags the voltage, in degrees.
items.s: tan(phi) = X/R = 6/10, so phi = 30.96 degrees.

items.q: A load takes 20 A from a 200 V supply at a power factor of 0.8. Calculate the real power in watts.
items.s: P = V I cos(phi) = 200 x 20 x 0.8 = 3200 W.

items.q: A circuit takes 5 A at 220 V. Calculate the apparent power in volt amperes.
An installation has an apparent power of 10000 VA and a real power of 4800 W. Calculate the reactive power in volt amperes reactive.
items.s: Q = root of (S squared - P squared) = root of (100000000 - 23040000) = 8773 VAR.

items.q: A load absorbs 6000 W while the apparent power drawn is 10000 VA. Calculate its power factor.
A series circuit has an inductance of 200 mH and a capacitance of 100 microfarads. Calculate the resonant frequency in hertz.
At resonance a coil has an inductive reactance of 100 ohms and a resistance of 25 ohms. Calculate the quality factor of the circuit.
A tuned circuit resonates at 100 kHz with a quality factor of 5. Calculate its bandwidth in kilohertz.
items.s: Bandwidth = fr/Q = 100/5 = 20 kHz.

items.q: A series resonant circuit has a resonant frequency of 800 kHz and a quality factor of 20. Calculate the upper half power frequency in kilohertz.
items.s: Half bandwidth = 800/(2 x 20) = 20 kHz, so the upper point is 820 kHz.

items.q: A coil of 400 turns carries a current of 1 A. Calculate the magnetomotive force in ampere turns.
items.s: F = N I = 400 x 1 = 400 ampere turns.

items.q: A magnetic circuit has a reluctance of 800 kilo ampere turns per weber and a magnetomotive force of 1500 ampere turns. Calculate the flux in milliwebers.
items.s: Flux = mmf/reluctance = 1500/(800 x 10^3) = 1.88 mWb.

items.q: Two coils of inductance 50 mH and 100 mH are coupled with a coupling coefficient of 0.5. Calculate their mutual inductance in millihenries.
items.s: M = k root of (L1 L2) = 0.5 x root of (50 x 100) = 35.36 mH = 35.35.
